html:
This chapter is about a line from a real plant. Cards with 64 wells come off a carousel feeder, get their wells filled from 64 bags of media, pass under a camera that checks every well against the product’s recipe, and either drop through a reject gate or go on to a tray of 130, which goes up one tower of a drying chamber and down the other. It started as a simulator Devon wrote of his own line, LineSim, with a calculator version and a PC version, and it is in Logix Connect as a classic scene, under File → New Project → Inspection line, with its guided track and its own faults. The model is LineSim’s, ported: the timing, the camera’s grey levels, the tracking, the dryer’s clock. What is new here is everything round it: the camera is the Vision Sensor that can talk to a real In-Sight, the recipe goes to it over TCP, and the machine is built to the model standard.

The machine

The cards start in the carousel feeder: 20 magazines of 200 blank cards round a turntable in front of the track, 4000 cards when it is full. The magazine at the feed station drops a card onto the feeder’s short track every pitch. When it is empty the turntable indexes the next full one round; for those few seconds a pitch or two go by with no card. When all 20 are empty the track runs on with nothing on it and the line shows MAGAZINES EMPTY until they are reloaded. The machine is a table, and its card track is an L: two straight tracks and a corner (Devon: “i just need the L shape”). Each track is a bed between black guide rails held by knurled knobs: white perforated plastic on the first two, and on the camera’s track strips of dark orange rubber either side of the card lane, for traction. Nothing moves the bed: the cards are pushed, and everything that pushes them is underneath. Under each track a Festo electric axis, as long as its stroke, carries a pneumatic lift cylinder and a finger. The finger lifts up through a slot in the bed behind the card at the drive’s pick place, the carriage runs forward one card width, pushing that card and the solid train ahead of it, then the finger drops below the bed and the carriage runs back while the cards stand (Devon: “the drives with fingers lift the finger from behind the card and push it forward”). M1’s drive is the smallest; M4’s the longest, since it pushes a row into the tray. Each drive has a job and waits on the next one. The feeder stands on the outside of the L at the start of the first track, and its own short Festo drive, M5, pushes each card off the magazine station sideways onto the track. M1 pushes the cards along the first track to the corner, and the filler head, M3, comes down and doses each one a pitch before the corner. Round the corner, M2 indexes them along the second track, past the laser marker, under the camera and over the reject gate, and on to the end sensor at the very end of the track, right before the tray. The cards stand nested, a card width apart, the whole length of the track: every drive pushes a solid train one card a stroke, its finger lifting behind the card at its pick place (M5 the feed place, M1 corner A, M2 corner B). The camera inspects each card as it stops in front of it; the gate, a card on, drops a failed one. When 13 stand on the end section, one at the end sensor and one at the 13th-card sensor, M4 takes them. With 13 at the end and a tray in position, the card picker M4, a Festo axis under the track in line with M2’s, lifts its finger behind the 13th card and shoves the 13 along the track’s end into the tray row in line with it, in one stroke; the finger drops and M4 runs home. M2 holds while the 13 stand and refills as soon as the pick slot is clear, before M4 is home. every one of these drives is a PLC output, so the program runs the line (below). The table feeds the loading conveyors in line: the transfer carries each full tray straight onto the first conveyor, and the four run on in a line to the chamber. The bag enclosure stands behind the camera’s track, beside the conveyors, and the lines to the head run across to it.

The camera and the UV laser marker stand on the back of the camera’s track, the enclosure side, and face the operator in front. The camera hangs from its mast over the cards. The marker is a big 3-axis head on an extrusion stand, with its scan nose over the track and the window on the nose’s underside; in the model it is the machine only, with no signals. The bag lines run up and over the marker’s head to the pump bank. At the filler, beside the first track on the outside of the L, a pitch before the corner, the head rides a vertical Festo electric axis (M3) down about three inches onto the card and doses every well the recipe fills, each from its own bag through its own pump and line. The bags hang in a glycol-cooled enclosure with clear doors, 8 by 4 feet, on a 2 ft platform; its lid lamps show where the recipe’s bags hang, and a well the recipe leaves empty gets an empty bag, so the enclosure shows the product’s layout, and its line runs clear. The 64 lines are clear tubes, so you see the media in each; a tube runs clear when its bag is empty. The enclosure has its own terminal, the Bag_HMI, with its own recipe sequence: load a recipe with the line stopped, hang the lit bags, BAGS HUNG, the lines prime, the chest cools, READY. Only then is Filler_Ready on.

The camera is the Vision Sensor, an In-Sight on module Cam1 in I/O Configuration, hanging from the line’s camera arm over a backlight. Backlit, a filled well reads dark (about 70) and an empty one light (about 220); the threshold, 100, splits them, or the Otsu option finds it from the card. A card on, right after the camera, the reject gate is a trap door in the track: it opens under a failed card and the card drops into the red bin. Good cards go on to the pick position, and M4 pushes them into the tray a row of 13 at a time, ten rows a tray. A full tray goes out onto four level loading conveyors, which carry it and hold it until the chamber takes it straight into the bottom of the load tower, which steps every rail up once a step (30 s); at the top it crosses into the unload tower, which steps down, and leaves at the bottom. With 130 rails a tower that is 2 h 10 min of drying; past the expiry (4 h) a tray comes out EXPIRED.

The tray loader and the loading conveyors

The trays are open aluminium ladder trays, a pocket for every card, 13 across and 10 rows. At the far end of the table a lift holds a stack of empty trays and raises the top one to the transfer level, a tray pitch at a time. The tray transfer is a square platen plate with four pneumatic grippers at its corners, on a carriage under one beam that runs over the centre line from the lift to the nest, on a portal at each end; an energy chain rides beside the beam. The platen comes down on the top empty tray on the lift, the grippers close on its rim, and it carries the tray over and sets it down in the nest, its first row in line with the card track, just past the track’s end. From there two index cylinders, one at each end of the tray, take over: each is a slide along the tray’s travel with a pawl that lifts behind the tray’s trailing rail. With the pawls up and M4’s fingers locked down on the tray, the indexers step it one row toward CONV 1 after every row M4 pushes in, so the next empty row lines up with the track (Tray_In_Pos is off while it moves). When the tenth row is in, the indexers run right through and push the full tray out onto the first loading conveyor (CONV 1, which has no lid), drop their pawls and run back behind the next empty tray the platen has meanwhile brought over. Devon: “The index cylinders push the tray ahead of the transfer, then get behind an empty tray the transfer brought over. The fingers lock down, then the indexers get behind the tray, lift, then index each slot until full, then push the tray to conveyor 1 and get behind the next empty tray.” M4’s fingers open when the tray is indexed and in fill position, and close and lift while it is indexing. The trays ride with their rows of 13 across the conveyors and the chamber. The loader is run by the PLC, by the Loader routine below, so every one of those moves is a rung you can read.

There are four loading conveyors, level, end to end, carrying the trays toward the chamber and holding them there: an enclosed module each, black side walls on legs, twin flat belts on a stainless bed, a hinged polycarbonate lid, a proximity sensor that sees the tray and a yellow bumper it stops against. They are numbered from the filler: CONV 1 takes the full tray from the nest and CONV 4 enters the chamber. They accumulate: a tray runs forward while the conveyor in front of it is clear, so while the chamber is waiting to step the trays fill CONV 4, then 3, 2 and 1. The chamber takes the tray on CONV 4 straight into the bottom of the load tower and every tray moves up one: a small pneumatic door, 2 inches tall and as wide as the conveyor, lifts, the tray runs in onto the bottom rail, and the door shuts behind it. If all four hold a tray, the full tray stays in the fill position, the rows wait and the drives stop short one after another: the whole line holds until the chamber steps. If the lift runs out of empty trays, the rows wait too and the line shows TRAY STACK EMPTY; REFILL STACK on the TRAY page loads it again. The number of empty trays on the lift is a setting on the line (20 to start).

Try it: run the carousel dry

On the FEEDER page press ONE MAGAZINE LEFT with the line running. The magazine at the track empties, the turntable goes looking for a full one and finds none: MAGAZINES EMPTY, and the Simulator Log says so. The track keeps running and the camera, the gate and the tray see nothing come. Press RELOAD MAGAZINES; the cards come again from the next pitch. Then reload and watch an ordinary magazine change: count the pitches with no card while the turntable indexes.

Try it: run the lift dry

In the line’s properties set the empty trays on the lift to 3 and run at 90 cards a minute. Three trays fill; then the rows stop, the TRAY page shows WAITING FOR THE LIFT and the Simulator Log shows TRAY STACK EMPTY. Press REFILL STACK and the next tray comes up and the rows start again. Before that, watch the track: 13 fill the end section and M2 holds with the stream behind them, because M4 cannot move without a tray. A blocked tray loader stops the whole line.

The recipe string: rows in, columns inspected

A product is one line of text: 1,SMP- GLD01,64,255,255,255,255,255,255,255,255,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000. The name and the 64 are not used by the inspection. The next eight numbers are the card’s rows, one byte each, row 1 first; the last eight are the no-test mask, laid out the same way. The card is numbered by columns: well 1 is at the bottom right of the card, well 8 at the top right; column 2 is wells 9 to 16, and so on to well 64 at the top left. So the string is sent in rows and the camera inspects in columns: well = (column − 1) × 8 + row, and column 1 is the 128 bit of every row byte, column 8 the 1 bit. A column is not one byte: it is the same bit of all eight.

Take a card whose rows read 254, 254, 254, 254, 254, 252, 252, 252. The 1 bit is off in every row, so column 8 is empty all the way up: wells 57 to 64. The 2 bit is off in rows 6 to 8 as well, so column 7 is empty at its top three wells: 54, 55, 56.

Byte C1 C2 C3 C4 C5 C6 C7 C8 128 64 32 16 8 4 2 1 Row 1 254 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 0 Row 2 254 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 0 Row 3 254 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 0 Row 4 254 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 0 Row 5 254 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 0 Row 6 252 1 1 1 1 1 1 0 0 Row 7 252 1 1 1 1 1 1 0 0 Row 8 252 1 1 1 1 1 1 0 0

A 1 in the no-test mask means that well is not inspected at all, whatever it holds; it does not mean "expect it empty". The page carries a sample set of made-up products and the test strings (Wells-Empty, Well-01 to Well-64, Wells-Filled); a real table loads from a text file with LOAD TABLE… and stays in that browser, never in the scene or the page.

The camera on Cam1, the string over TCP

The camera has to know what each card should hold, so the PLC sends it the card’s string as the card arrives, over a TCP Client Socket (Cam_Socket), the way the plant’s DVT camera gets it. The socket’s message is {card}, which becomes the string of the card at the camera. Then the PLC triggers the camera through its module’s tags. In the simulator the socket hands the string straight to the camera, and the camera judges the card under its lens with LineSim’s inspection; it answers on the socket in the DVT format, 1,NAME,64,PASS, and the eight row bytes it measured. With a real In-Sight on Cam1 and the socket going through the bridge, the same rungs run the real camera, and the real camera decides.

The program

The reference program is the line’s own rungs moved onto the camera module’s tags, with the stack light added, a routine that runs the five drives and one that runs the tray loader: six routines, forty-one rungs. File → Load Reference Solution: Inspection line loads it; Guide This Scene walks it with you, a lesson a routine (rung 0 and the JSRs; the drives; the loader; the camera; the tracking; the lamps), each lesson checking your routine against the reference and watching the line do what the rungs say: the platen grips a tray and carries it over, the tray indexes a row, a full tray goes out onto CONV 1.

MainRoutine

Rung 0 seals Line_Run in from START until STOP; then a JSR for each part of the job.

Drives

Each drive is run like a cylinder with two reed switches. Its output on carries the comb one pitch and holds it at the end (Mx_Ext); the rung lets go there, and the drive runs home with its pins down (Mx_Home). Every drive rung is the same shape: the conditions to start from home, a branch that holds the output on, and XIO(Mx_Ext) to let go. What differs is what each one waits for, and that is the machine’s order. M5 waits for corner A to be clear. M1 waits for the head to be up, its card dosed and corner B clear. The head waits for M1 to stop pushing, and M2 for a card in corner B and the camera’s answer. M4 waits for a full row and the tray in position: Row_Full comes on with 13 standing on the end section (the end sensor and the 13th-card sensor both made, M2’s stroke done), and M4 pushes the 13 into the tray row at once; a tray must be in position before M4 makes a move. Fill_Pending remembers that M1 has brought a card under the head, and M3_Done clears it. Cam_Wait holds M2 from the moment a card reaches the camera until Results_Valid, so the fail bit is always in Fail_Mem before M2’s index pulse shifts it, at any speed. The camera’s 0.5 s therefore sets the line’s top rate: about 75 cards a minute with the drives at 90. RunOut_TMR lets M2 index with no card in corner B after 1.5 s, so the last cards of a lot reach the row.

Loader

The loader is the same shape again: an output for each move, a switch at each end of it, and the rungs in the machine’s order. FULL TRAY OUT: with the tray’s ten rows in (Tray_Full), the pawls still up behind it and CONV 1 clear, Idx_Out latches and the indexers run right through, and Tray_Req asks for the next tray at the same moment, so the platen brings it over behind the full one going out (Devon: the indexers push the tray “ahead of the transfer”); at Idx_AtOut the tray is on the conveyor and the out stroke unlatches. GRIP waits for the platen at the stack and a tray up on the lift (Lift_Top), then closes the grippers; BRING IT OVER seals TT_Go in on TT_Gripped until the platen is over the nest, where SET DOWN opens the grippers once the nest is empty (Tray_Seated off), and the request clears with the tray in position. PAWLS UP lifts the pawls behind a seated tray and keeps them up through the out stroke; they drop while the platen is bringing a tray in and after each row step so the indexers can run back. INDEX: a one-shot on M4_Ext remembers a row placed (Row_Placed); with the pawls up and M4 home the indexers step a row (Idx_Step to Idx_Ext), and Row_Done holds the step until they are home again. LOCK closes M4’s fingers on the tray whenever it is moving or not in position. The whole routine runs on eleven inputs and six outputs, and every one of its times is a placeholder until it is measured.

Camera_Handshake

Triggering is enabled while the string link is up. The eye’s first scan on a card sends that card’s string and requests a trigger. A scan later (the string has gone) and with Trigger_Ready, the trigger latches; Trigger_Ack drops it. Half a second on, Results_Valid: with Job_Pass off the card failed, Fail_Mem latches, and the PLC acknowledges the result so the camera can present the next.

Reject_Tracking The gate is a card past the camera, so the fail has to travel with the card from the camera to the gate. Every M2 stroke moves every card one place, so one stroke is one shift. The index pulse comes once a pitch from M2’s stroke, 0.85 of a pitch along it, after the result is in: BSL shifts Fail_Mem into bit 0 of Fail_Track and moves the older cards on, and the next rung clears Fail_Mem for the next card. The card standing at the gate is bit 0, so the gate eye with bit 0 set opens the trap door; the next card’s result, latching Fail_Mem meanwhile, cannot touch it. The drying chamber on the terminal

The console (START, STOP, RESET), the camera’s socket and the three terminals stand on the open floor beside the bag enclosure, under the conveyors. The Operator View (Window menu) shows the line too: its screen is the Line_HMI’s pages, or the bag enclosure’s (Screen: Bag enclosure), and its control panel presses the console’s own START, STOP and RESET, with a RUNNING lamp on Line_Run and an ALARM lamp for any line alarm. The line’s own terminal (Line_HMI) has a page for each station. The DRYER page draws LineSim’s drying-chamber panel: the rails of both towers with their shelf tabs, every fifth numbered, each tray a bar on its rail with its number, product and load time, the step and the dryer log (FTI first tray in, LTI last tray in, FTO first out, LTO last out). With 130 rails a tower the page shows 17 at a time; ▲ and ▼ move the window, and the strip beside each tower shows all of them.

Try it: a recipe with empty wells

On the Bag_HMI open RECIPES with the line stopped, pick a product whose last row is 0 (the sample SMP-RED01), LOAD RECIPE, then BAGS HUNG on the SEQUENCE page. Watch the lid lamps: row 8 stays dark, no bags hang there, their tubes stay clear. Run the line and look at a card on the Cam_HMI: wells 8, 16 … 64 read light and are boxed grey, right as they are.

Try it: take an interlock out

In the Drives routine delete XIO(PE_CornerA) from the M5 rung and run. M5 now pushes while a card is still standing in corner A. The card behind stops against it, and so does the comb: M5 never reaches M5_Ext, its rung never lets go, and the plan shows M5 in red, STOPPED SHORT: CORNER A IS NOT CLEAR, until M1 clears the corner. Nothing breaks and nothing passes through anything, but the line has lost its rhythm. Put it back. Then take XIC(M3_Up)XIO(Fill_Pending) out of the M1 rung: M1 now pushes with the head down in a card and stops short at the head.

Try it: break the tracking

The tracking can only break with the old one-bit control, where the index does not wait for the camera. In the line’s properties set Drive control to Machine and load the reference solution again (it is the old program then), then set the rate to 90 cards a minute, Test Mode to 30 % and the index pulse to 0.5 pitch. Run it: the shift now comes before the result is in, so a card’s fail lands on the card behind it. Escapes (a bad card on the tray) and good cards dropped at the gate both count up on the LINE page. In this port it starts from about 70 cards a minute. Put the index back to 0.85 and they stop. With the PLC drives, Cam_Wait in the M2 rung does what the 0.85 does here, at every speed.

Try it: no string, no pass

Clear the socket’s message (or unplug the string link by giving Cam_Socket a message without {{card}}). The camera still triggers, but with no recipe it fails every card as NO STRING, and they all drop: good cards in the bin. That is why the camera setup rung enables triggering only while the link is up.

Watch For

The drive times are placeholders. A push takes half a card’s cycle (M2 0.35), the run back 0.3, the dose 0.35, scaled from the line rate; the picker takes 0.6 s in and 0.4 s back. With the PLC drives the rate setting is the drives’ speed, and the line makes what the handshakes allow. A drive that stops short is not a fault. It is waiting for the way to clear; the plan says which drive and why. If it never clears, look at the rung that should have waited. The loader’s times are placeholders. The platen’s 2.0 s over, 0.3 s to grip, 0.3 s for the pawls, 0.5 s a row step, 1.2 s out and 1.0 s back, the 3 s lift and the 20 trays on the lift are not measured on the real machine, nor the carousel’s 2.5 s index; change them when they are. A gap is not a fault. While the carousel indexes, pitches go by with no card. A program that counts index pulses as cards will be off by those gaps; count what the photo-eyes see. The bit order. Column 1 is the 128 bit of each row byte, column 8 the 1 bit. 254 is a row with column 8 empty, not column 1. A column is not a byte. The camera reads column by column, but the string holds rows: a column is the same bit of all eight bytes. The no-test mask skips a well. A 1 there means the well is not inspected; it does not mean the well should be empty. Send, then trigger. The trigger rung waits a scan after the send (XIO on the send bit), so the camera has the card’s string when it grabs the card. Clear the fail at the index. Without the OTU on the index pulse, one failed card keeps failing every card after it. Filler_Ready. Until the enclosure is READY the filler doses nothing; the cards go on dry and the camera fails them. Interlock the conveyor (or at least the alarm) on it.

Its faults

Faults → Inject has three for the line. Corrupted product strings: every eighth card’s string has its first byte off by one; the camera fails those cards as STRING != TABLE whatever the wells hold. The glycol supply stops: the chest warms, past 8 °C the Bag_HMI shows MEDIA WARM and Filler_Ready drops. The dryer stops stepping: the trays in it keep ageing, and those past the expiry come out EXPIRED when it steps again. The camera has its own alarms on the Vision Sensor: off line, a trigger while busy, a full results buffer.

rungs.head: Rung 0
rungs.comment: LINE RUN, SEAL-IN: START sets Line_Run and the rung holds itself in; STOP opens it. The five Festo drives run from it (rung 0 of the line's built-in program)

pred.q: Start_PB_Pressed is off, Line_Run is on and Stop_PB_Pressed is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Line_Run is on.

rungs.words: When either (Start_PB_Pressed (Start_PB Pressed: NO contact: 1 while pressed) is on) or (Line_Run (The line is running: START sets it, STOP drops it (the drives run from it)) is on) and Stop_PB_Pressed (Stop_PB Pressed: NO contact: 1 while pressed) is off, the rung turns Line_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Start_PB_Pressed) Examine If Closed asks: true when Start_PB_Pressed is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Line_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Line_Run is on.
  2. XIO(Stop_PB_Pressed) Examine If Open asks: true when Stop_PB_Pressed is off.
  3. OTE(Line_Run) Output Energize does: turns Line_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: The start condition turns Line_Run on, and Line_Run’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.
pats.think: a doorbell button and a hand. The start button is the doorbell, pressed for a moment. The seal-in contact is a hand that grabs the circuit as soon as the output comes on and keeps holding after you let go. The stop button, in series, is the only thing that can knock that hand away.
pats.watch: The stop has to be in series outside the branch. Put it inside the start path only and the seal-in path bypasses it: the stop no longer stops.

rungs.comment: The drives: M5, M1 and the filler M3, M2, the picker M4

  4. OTU(TT_Grip) Output Unlatch does: unlatches TT_Grip. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears TT_Grip when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Loader · Rung 5
rungs.comment: A TRAY IN THE NEST: the request is met; TT_Go drops and the platen goes back to the stack
rungs.words: When Tray_In_Pos (Line Tray_In_Pos: The tray in the nest is in position: an empty row lined up with the picker (off while it indexes a row and while trays swap)) is on and TT_AtNest (Line TT_AtNest: The transfer platen over the nest) is on, the rung unlatches Tray_Req (The nest needs a tray: set when the full one has gone out, cleared when the platen has set the new one down).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Tray_In_Pos) Examine If Closed asks: true when Tray_In_Pos is on.
  2. XIC(TT_AtNest) Examine If Closed asks: true when TT_AtNest is on.
  3. OTU(Tray_Req) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Tray_Req. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Tray_Req when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Loader · Rung 6
rungs.comment: PAWLS UP: a tray seated in the nest: the indexers lift their pawls behind its trailing rail, and keep them up through the out stroke; they drop for the run back after a row (Row_Done) and once the tray is on CONV 1

pred.q: Tray_Seated is on, Tray_Req is off, Row_Done is on, Idx_Out is off and Idx_AtOut is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Idx_Lift is off. None of the branch’s paths is true.

rungs.words: When either (Tray_Seated (Line Tray_Seated: A tray is seated in the nest (the nest sensor)) is on, Tray_Req (The nest needs a tray: set when the full one has gone out, cleared when the platen has set the new one down) is off and Row_Done (A row stroke is in: the pawls drop for the run back) is off) or (Idx_Out (Line Idx_Out: The indexers: run the full tray right through onto CONV 1) is on and Idx_AtOut (Line Idx_AtOut: The indexers at the end of the out stroke: the tray on CONV 1) is off), the rung turns Idx_Lift (Line Idx_Lift: The tray indexers: pawls up behind the tray (one each end)) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Tray_Seated) Examine If Closed asks: true when Tray_Seated is on.
    2. XIO(Tray_Req) Examine If Open asks: true when Tray_Req is off.
    3. XIO(Row_Done) Examine If Open asks: true when Row_Done is off.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Idx_Out) Examine If Closed asks: true when Idx_Out is on.
    2. XIO(Idx_AtOut) Examine If Open asks: true when Idx_AtOut is off.
  2. OTE(Idx_Lift) Output Energize does: turns Idx_Lift on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Loader · Rung 7
rungs.comment: A ROW PLACED: M4 at the end of its stroke (the row is in the tray): the tray is to index
rungs.words: When M4_Ext (Line M4_Ext: M4 at the end of its stroke: the row is in the tray) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung latches Row_Placed (M4 has placed a row and the tray is to index) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(M4_Ext) Examine If Closed asks: true when M4_Ext is on.
  2. ONS(Row_OS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Row_OS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. OTL(Row_Placed) Output Latch does: latches Row_Placed on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Row_Placed stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Loader · Rung 8
rungs.comment: INDEX A ROW: with M4 back home and the pawls up, stroke the tray one row; at Idx_Ext let go: the pawls drop, the indexers run back a row and lift again

pred.q: Row_Placed is off, Idx_Up is off, M4_Home is on, Tray_Full is on, Idx_Step is on and Idx_Ext is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Idx_Step is on.

rungs.words: When either (Row_Placed (M4 has placed a row and the tray is to index) is on, Idx_Up (Line Idx_Up: The indexers' pawls up behind the tray's trailing rail) is on, M4_Home (Line M4_Home: M4, the card picker, at the pick position) is on and Tray_Full (Line Tray_Full: The tray in the nest holds its 10 rows) is off) or (Idx_Step (Line Idx_Step: The indexers: stroke the tray one row forward and hold; off (pawls down) run back a row) is on) and Idx_Ext (Line Idx_Ext: The indexers at the end of a row stroke) is off, the rung turns Idx_Step on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Row_Placed) Examine If Closed asks: true when Row_Placed is on.
    2. XIC(Idx_Up) Examine If Closed asks: true when Idx_Up is on.
    3. XIC(M4_Home) Examine If Closed asks: true when M4_Home is on.
    4. XIO(Tray_Full) Examine If Open asks: true when Tray_Full is off.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Idx_Step) Examine If Closed asks: true when Idx_Step is on.
  2. XIO(Idx_Ext) Examine If Open asks: true when Idx_Ext is off.
  3. OTE(Idx_Step) Output Energize does: turns Idx_Step on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: The start condition turns Idx_Step on, and Idx_Step’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.

rungs.head: Loader · Rung 9
rungs.comment: ROW REQUEST CLEARED: the stroke is in, or the tray is full (its last row needs no index)
rungs.words: When either (Idx_Ext (Line Idx_Ext: The indexers at the end of a row stroke) is on) or (Tray_Full (Line Tray_Full: The tray in the nest holds its 10 rows) is on), the rung unlatches Row_Placed (M4 has placed a row and the tray is to index).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Idx_Ext) Examine If Closed asks: true when Idx_Ext is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Tray_Full) Examine If Closed asks: true when Tray_Full is on.
  2. OTU(Row_Placed) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Row_Placed. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Row_Placed when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Loader · Rung 10
rungs.comment: ROW DONE: the stroke is in: drop the pawls (Row_Done holds PAWLS UP off) for the run back

pred.q: Idx_Ext is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Row_Done is left as it was. It stops at XIC(Idx_Ext).

rungs.words: When Idx_Ext (Line Idx_Ext: The indexers at the end of a row stroke) is on, the rung latches Row_Done (A row stroke is in: the pawls drop for the run back) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Idx_Ext) Examine If Closed asks: true when Idx_Ext is on.
  2. OTL(Row_Done) Output Latch does: latches Row_Done on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Row_Done stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Loader · Rung 11
rungs.comment: BACK A ROW: the indexers home again behind the rail: the pawls lift
rungs.words: When Row_Done (A row stroke is in: the pawls drop for the run back) is on and Idx_Home (Line Idx_Home: The tray indexers at home: their pawls back at the nest's rear) is on, the rung unlatches Row_Done.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Row_Done) Examine If Closed asks: true when Row_Done is on.
  2. XIC(Idx_Home) Examine If Closed asks: true when Idx_Home is on.
  3. OTU(Row_Done) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Row_Done. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Row_Done when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Loader · Rung 12
rungs.comment: THE TRAY LOCK: M4's fingers close and lift while the tray moves or no tray is in position; open with the tray seated in fill position

pred.q: Idx_Step is off, Idx_Out is off and Tray_In_Pos is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Pick_Lock is on.

rungs.words: When either (Idx_Step (Line Idx_Step: The indexers: stroke the tray one row forward and hold; off (pawls down) run back a row) is on), (Idx_Out (Line Idx_Out: The indexers: run the full tray right through onto CONV 1) is on) or (Tray_In_Pos (Line Tray_In_Pos: The tray in the nest is in position: an empty row lined up with the picker (off while it indexes a row and while trays swap)) is off), the rung turns Pick_Lock (Line Pick_Lock: M4's fingers: close and lift to lock the tray while it indexes; open with the tray in fill position) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 3 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Idx_Step) Examine If Closed asks: true when Idx_Step is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Idx_Out) Examine If Closed asks: true when Idx_Out is on.
    Path 3
    1. XIO(Tray_In_Pos) Examine If Open asks: true when Tray_In_Pos is off.
  2. OTE(Pick_Lock) Output Energize does: turns Pick_Lock on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Camera_Handshake · Rung 0
rungs.comment: CAMERA SETUP: triggering enabled while the string link (the TCP socket to the camera) is up; results buffered, so none is overwritten while the program is busy

pred.q: Cam_Socket_Connected is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable is off and Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable is off. It stops at XIC(Cam_Socket_Connected).

rungs.words: When Cam_Socket_Connected (Cam_Socket Connected: TCP connection is up) is on, the rung turns Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false) and turns Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cam_Socket_Connected) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam_Socket_Connected is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable) Output Energize does: turns Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTE(Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable) Output Energize does: turns Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Camera_Handshake · Rung 1
rungs.comment: SEND THE STRING ON ARRIVAL: the first scan the eye sees a card, the socket sends that card's recipe string (1,NAME,64, 8 row bytes, 8 no-test bytes) to the camera, and a trigger is requested
rungs.words: When PE_Camera (Line PE_Camera: Photo-eye at the camera: a card is under the lens (within 6 u of it). The camera itself is the Vision Sensor (module Cam1)) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung turns Cam_Socket_Send (Cam_Socket Send: Rising edge sends the message) on (and off whenever the rung is false) and latches Trig_Req (A card is at the camera and its string has gone: trigger once the camera is ready) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Camera) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Camera is on.
  2. ONS(Send_OS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Send_OS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Cam_Socket_Send) Output Energize does: turns Cam_Socket_Send on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTL(Trig_Req) Output Latch does: latches Trig_Req on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Trig_Req stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Camera_Handshake · Rung 2
rungs.comment: TRIGGER once the string has gone (a scan after the send) and the camera says it can take one (Trigger_Ready): it grabs the card under the lens

pred.q: Trig_Req is on, Cam_Socket_Send is off and Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Cam1:O.Trigger latches on.

rungs.words: When Trig_Req (A card is at the camera and its string has gone: trigger once the camera is ready) is on, Cam_Socket_Send (Cam_Socket Send: Rising edge sends the message) is off and Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready is on, the rung latches Cam1:O.Trigger on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Trig_Req) Examine If Closed asks: true when Trig_Req is on.
  2. XIO(Cam_Socket_Send) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam_Socket_Send is off.
  3. XIC(Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready is on.
  4. OTL(Cam1:O.Trigger) Output Latch does: latches Cam1:O.Trigger on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Cam1:O.Trigger stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Camera_Handshake · Rung 3
rungs.comment: The camera has taken the trigger (Trigger_Ack): drop it and the request
rungs.words: When Cam1:I.Trigger_Ack is on, the rung unlatches Cam1:O.Trigger and unlatches Trig_Req (A card is at the camera and its string has gone: trigger once the camera is ready).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cam1:I.Trigger_Ack) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Trigger_Ack is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(Cam1:O.Trigger) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cam1:O.Trigger. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Trig_Req) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Trig_Req. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Cam1:O.Trigger when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Camera_Handshake · Rung 4
rungs.comment: THE RESULT: Results_Valid with Job_Pass off is a FAIL: remember it; acknowledge the result so the camera can present the next

pred.q: Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on, Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is on and Cam1:I.Job_Pass is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Fail_Mem is left as it was and Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is left as it was. It stops at XIO(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack).

rungs.words: When Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on and Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is off, each path is tested on its own: if Cam1:I.Job_Pass is off, it latches Fail_Mem (The camera said FAIL for the card it just inspected (latched until the next index pulse)) on; it latches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cam1:I.Results_Valid) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on.
  2. XIO(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is off.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. XIO(Cam1:I.Job_Pass) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:I.Job_Pass is off.
    2. OTL(Fail_Mem) Output Latch does: latches Fail_Mem on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 2
    1. OTL(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack) Output Latch does: latches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Fail_Mem stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Camera_Handshake · Rung 5
rungs.comment: The camera has taken the acknowledge (Results_Valid off): ready for the next result
rungs.words: When Cam1:I.Results_Valid is off, the rung unlatches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Cam1:I.Results_Valid) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:I.Results_Valid is off.
  2. OTU(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.
